Any endpoints A,B have those heights. Their midpoint O has height zero and lies in gamma; opposite nonzero endpoint heights imply a unique crossing at O.

exercise_reviews.independent_solution: Using m-vector=AM, d-vector=MN, n-vector=NB, the polygon rule gives AB=m-vector+d-vector+n-vector. The two d cross-terms vanish because MN is a common perpendicular. Therefore |AB|^2=m^2+d^2+n^2+2 m-vector dot n-vector. Directed angles phi and 180 degrees minus phi give the plus and minus cross-terms for complete cases a),b), respectively.
